evidence: learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/usp10/ns-usp10-script_tabdef documents a negative tab stop only as far-edge alignment ('Positive values represent near-edge alignment, while negative values represent far-edge alignment') without saying what width the tab character itself gets; far-edge alignment ends the following text at the stop, which needs the width of the text after the tab, and getGivenTabWidth sees only the tab position. usp10 tests/usp10.c has no SSA_TAB or SCRIPT_TABDEF use (grep count 0), so no Windows ground truth either. Undocumented algorithm AND untested; the case (cTabStops == 1 with a negative first stop) is rare. Left as the FIXME.
